title: Practitioner Exam
description: 40 questions covering all five modules, drawn from a pool of 50. Pass mark is 80%. This is an open-book exam — take your time, browse any module to refresh your memory, or ask the AI assistant for help. Your answers are saved as you go, so leaving the page to look something up is fine. Explanations show after submission so you can learn from any answers you missed.

questions.scenario: A transformation executes successfully on one developer's machine but fails with a file-not-found error when run by a colleague. Both users are using the same transformation file (.ktr) and have access to the same shared source files.
questions.prompt: What is the most probable reason for this discrepancy?
options: The colleague is using a different version of Spoon, causing it to interpret step settings, including file paths, incorrectly.
The source file requires re-importation into Spoon on each machine before it can be accessed by the transformation.
A configured file path relies on a variable defined in a .properties file, and this variable has a different value or is not defined on the colleague's machine.
The transformation file (.ktr) contains absolute file paths, making it non-portable and restricted to the environment where it was originally created.
questions.explanation: The path relies on a **variable** defined in `kettle.properties`, which lives in each user's own `.kettle` folder, so the variable can resolve to a different folder, or to nothing at all, on another machine.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Configuring PDI

questions.scenario: A development team needs to define a standard database hostname and an input folder path for all Pentaho Data Integration (PDI) transformations and jobs running on each server. They want to avoid hard-coding these values directly into each transformation or job.
questions.prompt: Which configuration file should be used to store these values so they can be referenced across all PDI jobs and transformations on a given machine?
options: `kettle.properties`
`repositories.xml`
`.spoonrc`
`shared.xml`
questions.explanation:
The `kettle.properties` file is loaded by PDI at startup and allows for the definition of **configuration variables** that can be used throughout transformations and jobs using the `${variable_name}` syntax.

By defining values in this file, the system can reference global settings like hostnames or paths without requiring these values to be hard-coded in individual components.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Kettle Variables

questions.scenario: A data integration developer is configuring a Text file input step in Pentaho Data Integration (PDI). The desired input file path should be dynamically determined at runtime using a Kettle variable named INPUT_PATH, rather than being hardcoded within the step configuration.
questions.prompt: Which expression should be used in the Filename field of the Text file input step to reference the value of the INPUT_PATH variable?
options: `$INPUT_PATH$`
`%INPUT_PATH%`
`@INPUT_PATH`
`${INPUT_PATH}`
questions.explanation: `${INPUT_PATH}` is PDI's **variable syntax**: the `${}` notation tells PDI to resolve the variable at runtime.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Kettle Variables

questions.scenario: A Pentaho Data Integration developer modifies the `kettle.properties` file on their Windows workstation to adjust a system-level setting. After restarting Spoon, the change is not reflected in the application's behavior, leading them to suspect an issue with the configuration file location.
questions.prompt: By default, where does Pentaho Data Integration (PDI) locate the `kettle.properties` file on a Windows system?
options: %USERPROFILE%\.kettle\kettle.properties
%APPDATA%\Pentaho\kettle.properties
C:\Pentaho\design-tools\data-integration\kettle.properties
C:\ProgramData\Pentaho\kettle.properties
questions.explanation:
Pentaho Data Integration (PDI) prioritizes the `kettle.properties` file located in the **user home directory**, specifically within the `.kettle` folder.

This specific path allows for **user-specific configurations** to be maintained independently of the installation directory or system-wide settings.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Kettle Variables

questions.scenario: A data engineer opens Spoon to start a new transformation. Instead of the design canvas, the window shows a table of scheduled runs.
questions.prompt: Which perspective must be selected to access the transformation design canvas?
options: Scheduler
Data Integration
Welcome page
Model
questions.explanation: The **Data Integration** perspective is the design canvas for transformations and jobs.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Getting Started — Configuring PDI

questions.scenario: A Pentaho Data Integration (PDI) transformation is designed to process customer data from a text file. A transformation designer has connected a Text file input step directly to a Filter rows step using a hop.
questions.prompt: What is the primary function of the hop between the Text file input step and the Filter rows step when the transformation executes?
options: The hop carries rows read from the text file to the filter for evaluation.
The hop schedules the filter step to run after the text file input is complete.
The hop re-reads the text file if the filter encounters an error.
The hop copies configuration parameters from the input step to the filter step.
questions.explanation:
A **hop** defines the flow of data between steps in a transformation. It carries rows read from the source to the subsequent step for evaluation.

Text file input → Filter rows
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Hello World

questions.scenario: A data integration specialist is building a transformation with several steps and needs to check the rows coming out of step four without waiting for the whole transformation to finish.
questions.prompt: What primary function does the Preview feature provide that a standard Run execution does not?
options: It runs faster than a normal execution by skipping data validation checks.
It runs the whole transformation but suppresses all writing to output files.
It captures the rows a chosen step produces and pauses the run once enough rows are collected.
It generates sample rows from the transformation's logic without processing real data.
questions.explanation:
The **Preview** feature initiates the transformation and captures the rows produced by the selected step, pausing the execution once the specified number of rows is gathered. This allows the developer to see the data at a specific point in the transformation without running the entire process to completion.

Unlike a standard run, which processes all data through all steps, a preview focuses on a **limited sample** of rows from a specific point to facilitate debugging and verification.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Hello World

questions.scenario: A data integration developer is troubleshooting a transformation that processes sensitive customer data. They need to examine the data flowing through each step to identify the source of a data quality issue.
questions.prompt: Which logging level will capture the actual data values for each row as the transformation executes?
options: Detailed
Basic
Row Level
Debug
questions.explanation: The **Row Level** logging level provides the most granular output because it includes the contents of each row as it passes through each step of the transformation.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Logging

questions.scenario: A transformation reads data from a source and sends it to two downstream steps: one writes the data to a text file, and the other inserts it into a database table. When defining the second hop from the initial step, the Copy option is selected in the dialog box.
questions.prompt: How does the Copy hop type determine the flow of data to the connected steps?
options: Each row of data is sent to both the file writing step and the database table step.
The transformation will fail, as a step can only have one output hop.
Data is sent alternately to the file writing step, then the database table step, repeating until all rows are processed.
Only the first step connected to the source step will receive any data.
questions.explanation: The **Copy** hop type duplicates the data stream, so every row is sent to every connected step: here, both the text file and the database table.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology

questions.scenario: A data integration specialist is building a transformation to process customer records. The specialist needs detailed logging of specific field values as the data flows through the transformation to help with debugging and monitoring data quality.
questions.prompt: Which transformation step is designed to write custom messages, including field values, to the execution log for each processed row?
options: Set variables, with a message field
Text file output, configured to append to a log file
Write to log
Abort, configured to include a diagnostic message
questions.explanation: The **Write to log** step is specifically designed to output custom messages to the execution log. It allows the developer to include specific field values for every row processed during the transformation.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Logging

questions.scenario: A data integration process uses a Table output step configured to handle errors. When an attempt to insert a row into the target database fails, the row is routed to an error handling hop, appending data to a designated text file for review.
questions.prompt: What information is included in each row written to the error file?
options: Only the error message, presented as a single field within the error file row.
The Java exception stack trace generated when the insertion attempt failed.
The complete row data, along with fields containing the error description, error codes, and the specific fields that caused the error.
Only the row's key fields and an error flag.
questions.explanation: The **error handling hop** captures the entire original row and appends technical details regarding the failure. These details include the error description, error codes, and the specific fields that caused the error, as defined in the configuration of the step.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Error Handling

questions.scenario: A nightly load can meet two kinds of trouble: a handful of rows failing validation, and the source file arriving with zero rows when 1,000 were expected.
questions.prompt: Which of the two should the Abort step handle?
options: The failing rows, as Abort is how rows are diverted
Neither, as Abort stops only the step it sits in
The empty file, since loading it would wipe good data
Both, as Abort is how any error should be handled
questions.explanation:
An empty file represents a **bad run** rather than a bad row; loading such a file would quietly replace existing data with nothing, making an **Abort** step the correct way to stop the entire process.

While individual rows may fail validation, these should be handled by routing them to a separate branch so the remaining valid rows can still be processed.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Error Handling

questions.scenario: A Calculator step in the middle of a transformation produces unexpected totals. You want to view the rows it outputs without running the transformation to the end.
questions.prompt: How do you do that in Spoon?
options: Open the Calculator in a separate workspace.
Run the transformation and read the log.
Add a text file output and run to the end.
Select the Calculator step and preview it.
questions.explanation: **Preview** shows the rows a step outputs and pauses the run once enough have been collected, so the Calculator's output can be inspected without running the transformation to the end.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Concepts & Terminology — Hello World

questions.scenario: A CSV file is read with a Text file input step, and its first line holds column names rather than data.
questions.prompt: How do you configure the step to treat the first line as a header?
options: Enable Lazy conversion on the Content tab
Run Get Fields with the first row selected
Drop the first row with Filter rows
Tick Header on the Content tab
questions.explanation: Ticking **Header** on the Content tab, with one header line, tells the step to read the first line as field names rather than data.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Text File Input

questions.scenario: An `orders.json` document contains an array under `orders`, and each order contains a nested customer object with an `email` field. A JSON input step is configured to read one row per order.
questions.prompt: Which expression reads each order's customer email?
options: orders.customer.email
/orders/order/customer/email
$.orders[*].customer.email
$.customer.email[*]
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Read JSON

questions.scenario: A supplier sends invoices as XML containing an `<invoices>` root holding `<invoice>` elements, each with an `<amount>` child. The Get data from XML step is configured to read one row per invoice.
questions.prompt: What should the step use as its loop path?
options: `$.invoices.invoice[*]`
`/invoices/invoice`
`//amount`
`invoices > invoice`
questions.explanation:
The **loop path** is an XPath expression that identifies the repeating element within the XML structure, such as `/invoices/invoice`.

By defining the loop path, the step determines the level at which it iterates to create rows, ensuring that fields like `amount` are retrieved relative to each specific invoice.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Read XML

questions.scenario: A load into a customer table must update a customer's row if its key already exists, or insert a new row if it does not.
questions.prompt: Which step does both, based on the key?
options: Combination lookup/update
Insert / update
Table output
Update
questions.explanation: The **Insert / update** step looks each row up by its key, updates the row if it finds one, and inserts it if not.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Table Insert/Update

questions.scenario: Finance requests the region where a customer resided on 1 March, even though the customer has moved since that date. The customer dimension is maintained as a Type 2 slowly changing dimension.
questions.prompt: Why can the dimension answer that?
options: It keeps a row per version, each with valid dates.
It keeps only the changes since the last load.
It keeps a version flag per row, but no dates.
It keeps the latest value, overwritten in place.
questions.explanation: A Type 2 **slowly changing dimension** maintains a historical record by creating a new row for every change. Each row includes specific **valid dates**, which allows a query to identify the specific record that was active at any point in the past.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Slowly Changing Dimensions

questions.scenario: A developer needs to read and write objects in a MinIO bucket running on-premises.
questions.prompt: How do you connect PDI to that bucket?
options: Create an S3-compatible VFS connection to MinIO
Use an HDFS path in the Hadoop file input step
Create a JDBC connection to the MinIO server
Install a dedicated MinIO plugin from Marketplace
questions.explanation: Because MinIO uses the S3 protocol, a connection configured as an **S3-compatible VFS** allows PDI to read and write data to the bucket exactly as it would with AWS S3.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — MinIO

questions.scenario: The first step of a new transformation must take the rows returned by a SELECT query that joins two tables in a PostgreSQL source.
questions.prompt: Which step runs that query and passes its rows downstream?
options: Database lookup
Database join
Execute SQL script
Table input
questions.explanation: The **Table input** step runs a SELECT against a database connection and emits each result row, so it starts a stream.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Reading from a Database

questions.scenario: A monthly transformation writes to an Excel workbook, and each run must add its rows below the previous month's rather than replacing the file.
questions.prompt: How do you configure the Microsoft Excel writer step?
options: Reuse the file and sheet, starting at the sheet's end
Replace the output file on every run
Use Text file output with an .xlsx extension
Write a new workbook with the date in its name
questions.explanation: The **Microsoft Excel writer** can reuse the existing file and sheet and start writing at the end of the sheet, so the new rows are appended below last month's.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Excel Writer

questions.scenario: A nightly export produces millions of rows, and the team wants each output file capped at a manageable number of rows.
questions.prompt: Which Text file output setting does that?
options: Buffer size, set to the file size wanted
Add date to filename, for a file per run
Limit, set to the maximum rows to write
Split every ... rows, set to the row limit
questions.explanation: **Split every ... rows** starts a new output file after that many rows, so each file stays capped.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Text File Output

questions.scenario: A developer sets up a new connection to a MySQL database, but Spoon reports that the driver cannot be found.
questions.prompt: What must be added for PDI to connect?
options: An ODBC data source for the MySQL server
The MySQL JDBC driver JAR, in data-integration/lib
The MySQL command-line client, on the PATH
A MySQL connector plugin from Marketplace
questions.explanation:
Pentaho Data Integration connects to databases via **JDBC**, and since the MySQL driver is not bundled with the software, the JAR file must be placed in the `data-integration/lib` directory.

After placing the driver in the correct directory, the application must be restarted for the connection to be recognized.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Connecting to a Database

questions.scenario: An orders stream is joined to a customers stream using a Merge join on `customer_id`. The orders are provided by a Table input with no `ORDER BY` clause, and the customers are provided by a CSV file read in file order.
questions.prompt: What must be true of both inputs before the join?
options: Both have unique `customer_id` values.
Both come from the same database connection.
Both are sorted on `customer_id`, in the same direction.
Both have the same number of rows.
questions.explanation: The **Merge join** step walks the two streams in step, so both must be **sorted** on the join key in the same direction. Here that means an `ORDER BY` in the query and a Sort rows step after the CSV.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Merge Join

questions.scenario: A fact table contains four low-cardinality flags: payment type, channel, promotion, and gift wrap. The warehouse design folds these attributes into one junk dimension with a surrogate key for every unique combination.
questions.prompt: Which step maintains that dimension?
options: Dimension lookup/update
Combination lookup/update
Database lookup
Insert / update
questions.explanation: The **Combination lookup/update** step assigns a surrogate key to each new combination of its input fields and reuses that key when the combination appears again, which is exactly a junk dimension.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Slowly Changing Dimensions

questions.scenario: A CSV file contains text fields wrapped in double quotes because those fields contain commas.
questions.prompt: Which Text file input setting reads those fields correctly?
options: Separator, set to a character never used
Enclosure, set to the double quote
Escape, set to the comma
Lazy conversion, turned off
questions.explanation: The **Enclosure** setting identifies the character that wraps a field. This ensures that any commas contained within those wrapping characters are treated as part of the data rather than as delimiters.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Data Sources — Text File Input

questions.scenario: You must enrich 5 million order rows with customer data from a 2-million-row database table. A colleague suggests a Database join; you are weighing it against a Merge join.
questions.prompt: Which two statements correctly contrast the Database join and Merge join steps?
options: Merge join requires both inputs to be sorted on the join key.
Database join is faster than Merge join at this size.
Database join requires its input to be sorted on the join key.
Merge join executes a SQL query for each incoming row.
Database join executes a SQL query for each incoming row.
questions.explanation:
The **Merge join** step requires both input streams to be sorted on the join key before the join operation can be performed.

The **Database join** step functions by executing a separate SQL query for every incoming row in the stream, which provides flexibility but results in a high volume of individual queries when processing large datasets.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Database Join

questions.scenario: A transformation intended to output 5,000 rows produces several million rows, and the run never finishes.
questions.prompt: Which step most likely explains this behavior?
options: Merge join, duplicating rows from an unsorted input
Stream lookup, returning every row that matches a key
Join rows, emitting every combination of its two inputs
Database join, re-querying and multiplying each row
questions.explanation: **Join rows** produces the Cartesian product, every row of one input paired with every row of the other, so 2,000 rows against 2,500 already makes 5,000,000. It usually means the step was used where a keyed join was meant.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Join Rows

questions.scenario: A transformation processes millions of rows through a Database lookup against a small, static reference table. The developer wants to reduce the number of round-trips to the database.
questions.prompt: What does enabling the lookup cache avoid?
options: Schema validation errors on the lookup table
Repeating a query for a key it has already seen
Running out of connections in the pool
Race conditions between concurrent step copies
questions.explanation: By enabling the **lookup cache**, the result of each lookup is stored in memory. This ensures that if a key is encountered again, the result is retrieved from the cache rather than executing another query against the database.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Database Lookups

questions.scenario: A user compares yesterday's customer extract, the reference stream, with today's, the compare stream, using the Merge rows (diff) step. Customer 1042 is in yesterday's extract but missing from today's.
questions.prompt: Which flag does Merge rows (diff) give that customer?
options: removed
changed
new
deleted
questions.explanation: The **Merge rows (diff)** step identifies records that are present in the reference stream but absent from the compare stream and assigns them the flag `deleted`.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Merge Rows (diff)

questions.scenario: An analyst provides pricing rules written as spreadsheet formulas, such as `IF([qty] > 100; [bulk_price]; [list_price])`, and wants them to be implemented in a transformation as written.
questions.prompt: Which step evaluates those expressions most directly?
options: User defined Java class
Formula
Calculator
Modified JavaScript value
questions.explanation: The **Formula** step evaluates spreadsheet-style expressions, such as `IF`, where fields are referenced in square brackets. This allows the rules to be carried into the transformation with minimal changes to the original logic.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Formula

questions.scenario: An e-commerce company receives a high-volume stream of order data, and each order includes a two-letter country code. The company needs to enrich each order with the full country name from a static list of valid country codes.
questions.prompt: Which characteristic makes Stream lookup the most efficient method for this enrichment?
options: The reference data set is small enough to be fully cached in memory, enabling very fast lookups.
Stream lookup automatically handles updates to the reference data set without requiring a restart.
Stream lookup is optimized to handle large reference data sets that exceed available memory.
Stream lookup can return multiple matching country names for a single country code.
questions.explanation: The **Stream lookup** step is highly efficient because it loads the entire reference data set into memory at the start of the transformation. This caching allows the engine to perform very fast lookups for each incoming row without hitting a database or file for every record.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Lookups

questions.scenario: A Group by step totals sales per region, but the output lists the North region several times, each with a partial total.
questions.prompt: What is missing upstream of the Group by step?
options: A Sort rows step on the region field
A limit on the number of input rows
A Select values step aligning the types
An aggregation that pre-sums each region
questions.explanation: The Group by step aggregates **consecutive rows** that share the same key value. If the input data is not ordered, a single region may appear in multiple non-contiguous blocks, causing the step to treat them as separate groups. Applying a Sort rows step ensures all rows for a specific region are adjacent, allowing the Group by step to calculate a single total for that region.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset

questions.scenario: A new rule sets a discount from several conditions together: the customer's tier, the order size, and whether the order date falls in a promotion window.
questions.prompt: Why does this rule call for Modified JavaScript value rather than Calculator?
options: Calculator works on batches, not single rows.
It runs faster than Calculator on every row.
Calculator can only handle numeric fields.
It can express arbitrary per-row logic with conditions.
questions.explanation:
The **Modified JavaScript value** step runs full per-row logic, so nested conditions across several fields are straightforward.

Calculator offers only a fixed list of operations.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset — Modified JavaScript Value

questions.scenario: A data stream contains duplicate records based on a key field, and the records arrive in no particular order.
questions.prompt: Which steps remove the duplicates correctly?
options: Select values with the key marked unique
Stream lookup of the stream against itself
Unique rows on its own, keyed on the field
Sort rows on the key, then Unique rows
questions.explanation:
The **Unique rows** step compares each row only with the row immediately preceding it in the stream. By using a **Sort rows** step first, all identical keys are grouped together, ensuring that the **Unique rows** step can identify and remove all duplicates.

Alternatively, the Unique rows (HashSet) variant can identify duplicates without a prior sort, but it requires more memory to maintain the set of seen values.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset

questions.scenario: A Filter rows step checks `qty > 0`. One step is connected for orders with a quantity, and another for orders without.
questions.prompt: How does Filter rows route the orders?
options: All rows continue, each flagged true or false
True rows to one step, false rows to the other
Matching rows continue; the rest are dropped
Non-matching rows continue; the rest are dropped
questions.explanation: Filter rows has a **true hop** and a **false hop**, and with both connected, each order goes to exactly one of the two steps.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enriching the Dataset

questions.scenario: A data integration specialist is building a Pentaho Data Integration transformation to calculate a discount based on customer loyalty status. The discount amount must be dynamically calculated for each customer record as part of a larger data flow.
questions.prompt: Within a PDI transformation, what is the primary function of the Formula step?
options: The Formula step establishes connections to relational databases for direct data retrieval.
The Formula step provides a mechanism for generating synthetic data to validate transformation logic.
The Formula step automatically categorizes and tags fields based on their data type.
The Formula step evaluates Formula Expressions to derive new field values.
questions.explanation:
The Formula step evaluates **Formula Expressions** to derive new field values. It is used to perform calculations and create derived data within a stream.

This step allows for the dynamic generation of values based on existing fields, which is essential when calculating variables like discounts or status flags for each record in a transformation.
questions.source: Formula

questions.scenario: A data analyst needs to enrich a dataset with information from a database based on values within each row of the incoming data.
questions.prompt: What is a key characteristic of the Database join step in Pentaho Data Integration?
options: It runs a query for each input row and appends every row returned to a copy of that row.
It classifies the data automatically for easier search and retrieval.
It is most efficient when processing millions of rows of data.
It merges tables inside the database using standard join operations.
questions.explanation:
The Database join step performs a **parameterized query** for every individual row received from the input stream.

For every result returned by the database for a specific input row, the step appends a copy of that input row to the result set.
questions.source: Database Join

questions.scenario: A nightly process must download a file, load it with two transformations in order, and email the team if either load fails.
questions.prompt: Why is this built as a job rather than a transformation?
options: A job processes the file's rows faster
A transformation cannot accept parameters
A transformation cannot read downloaded files
A job sequences entries and branches on the outcome
questions.explanation:
A job is designed to **orchestrate** a workflow. It executes entries in a specific sequence, such as a download, multiple transformations, and a mail notification, while managing the logic of the process by following success or failure hops.

Unlike a transformation, which processes data row by row, a job manages the high-level execution flow of the overall process.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Hello World Job

questions.scenario: In a job, a developer wants a follow-on entry to run only when the preceding entry completes successfully.
questions.prompt: Which kind of hop should connect the two entries?
options: A hop followed only on a false result
An unconditional hop
A hop from an entry set to run in parallel
A hop followed only when the result is true
questions.explanation: A hop evaluated on a **true result**, shown green, runs the next entry only when the previous entry succeeded.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Order of Execution

questions.scenario: A data pipeline uses a transformation that expects an input folder location. This location is defined by a parameter named `IN_DIR`. The transformation is executed both by a nightly batch job and interactively from the command line using Pan, often with different folder paths each time.
questions.prompt: How does the transformation resolve the correct input folder location for each execution?
options: The transformation reads the input folder path from the first row of data in the input stream.
The transformation uses the value of the `IN_DIR` parameter, which is set by the calling process at runtime.
The transformation retrieves the input folder path from a pre-configured value within the .ktr file.
The transformation obtains the input folder path from the `kettle.properties` file on the server hosting the transformation.
questions.explanation:
The transformation uses the value of the `IN_DIR` parameter, which is set by the calling process at runtime.

**Parameters** allow external control of transformation behavior, and their values are supplied when the transformation runs.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Parameters

questions.scenario: You are creating a run configuration in Spoon for a transformation that must run on a remote Carte server rather than on your laptop.
questions.prompt: What should the run configuration target?
options: The repository, which forwards the run to Carte
Pentaho local, with the Carte host in a variable
An embedded JVM container on the remote host
The Pentaho engine, running on the Carte server
questions.explanation: A **run configuration** targets the Pentaho engine either locally or on a remote Carte server, so choosing the Carte server sends the run there.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Run Configurations

questions.scenario: A scheduler on a Linux server with no Spoon installed must run a nightly job (.kjb) and, separately, a standalone transformation (.ktr).
questions.prompt: Which command-line APIs run them?
options: spoon.sh in headless mode, for both of them
Pan for the job, and Kitchen for the transformation
Kitchen for the job, and Pan for the transformation
Carte for both, started once as a service
questions.explanation:
The **Kitchen** utility is used to execute job files (.kjb) from the command line, while the **Pan** utility is used to execute transformation files (.ktr).

Both tools execute the processes to completion, making them suitable for use with an automated scheduler in a headless environment.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Run Configurations

questions.scenario: A transformation declares a parameter named `REGION`. It is sometimes run with no value supplied, and must then use the default value of EMEA.
questions.prompt: Where is that default value set?
options: In a Set variables step at the transformation's start
On the Parameters tab of each calling job
On the Parameters tab of the transformation's settings
In kettle.properties on the host that runs it
questions.explanation: A parameter's default is declared on the **Parameters tab** of the transformation's own properties, and it is used whenever no caller supplies a value.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Parameters

questions.scenario: The operations team wants an email automatically each time the nightly load job finishes.
questions.prompt: Which job entry sends that email?
options: HTTP
Mail validator
Mail
Write to log
questions.explanation: The **Mail** entry sends an SMTP message and is usually placed on the success or failure hop of the entry that matters.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Jobs

questions.scenario: An administrator adds `DB_HOST` to `kettle.properties` on the server. A job and the three transformations it calls all reference `${DB_HOST}`.
questions.prompt: Where is `DB_HOST` available when the job runs?
options: In the three transformations, but not the job
In the job and in all three transformations
Only after a Set variables step has run
Only on the master node in a clustered run
questions.explanation:
Variables defined in `kettle.properties` are loaded when Pentaho Data Integration starts and are available to every job and transformation in that process, providing a **global scope**.

Because these variables are loaded globally at the start of the process, they do not require a Set variables step to be accessible by subsequent components.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Parameters and Variables

questions.scenario: Four developers work on the same transformations and the team performs all code reviews through Git.
questions.prompt: Which repository choice fits this team best?
options: File-based, giving up the database's locking and shared security
Either one, since the choice has no effect on collaboration
File-based, the only option that works without a server
Database-backed, the only option for several developers
questions.explanation:
A **file-based repository** is a folder of `.ktr` and `.kjb` files, so the team's existing branching, review, and history in Git apply to pipelines too.

What it gives up is the database repository's **record locking**, shared connections, and central permissions.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution

questions.scenario: Operations require one tool to execute a nightly job via a cron schedule and then exit, and another tool to remain running to accept remote transformations over HTTP.
questions.prompt: Which Pentaho services are suitable for each role?
options: Kitchen runs the job and exits; Carte stays up for HTTP
Pan runs the job and exits; Kitchen stays up for HTTP
Kitchen fills both roles, started with a service flag
Carte runs the job and exits; Kitchen stays up for HTTP
questions.explanation:
The **Kitchen** service is designed to execute a job to completion and then exit, making it the appropriate choice for a cron-scheduled task.

In contrast, **Carte** is a long-running server that remains active to accept and execute transformations over HTTP, supporting remote and clustered execution.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Run Configurations

questions.scenario: A clustered transformation runs across one Carte master and two slave servers. The heavy aggregation steps in the transformation are marked as clustered.
questions.prompt: What does the master do during the run?
options: Only stores the logs that the slaves write
Distributes rows to the slaves and gathers their results
Processes every row itself while the slaves wait
Holds the database connection pool for the slaves
questions.explanation: The master coordinates: it **distributes rows** to the slave servers, which do the heavy work in parallel, and gathers their results into a single stream.
questions.source: Pentaho Developer - Practitioner: Enterprise Solution — Run Configurations

questions.scenario: A data integration developer is setting up a new workstation and wants to ensure the Pentaho Data Integration (PDI) environment is optimized for rapid development, especially given a database schema that changes frequently.
questions.prompt: Which option, when disabled in Spoon's General settings, would be most beneficial in this scenario?
options: Show welcome page at startup
Use database cache
Ask user when exiting
Show repository dialog at startup
questions.explanation: Disabling the **Use database cache** option ensures that Spoon re-reads the live schema every time a dialog is opened. This is beneficial when the underlying database schema changes frequently, as it prevents the software from relying on outdated metadata stored in the cache.
questions.source: Configuring PDI
